policy.title: Benchmark evidence policy
policy.summary: Benchmarks are supporting evidence, not our final ranking. We identify the exact model/version, source, snapshot date and harness. Product scores are not treated as model scores, and results from different harness versions are not compared directly.

sources.name: Arena Text Leaderboard
sources.measures: Human preference in anonymous model-vs-model battles across open-ended text tasks.
sources.caveat: A product such as ChatGPT or Claude can change its default model; Arena ranks specific model versions, not the whole product. Checked 2026-09-14 and re-checked 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-28: the text leaderboard served snapshot id "latest" dated 2026-09-25 (vote cutoff 2026-09-25T22:00:00.000Z, 8,528,723 votes, 409 models), read through the canonical route, the alternate text-overall route and the embedded data payload, all agreeing. Every tracked row was re-read from that snapshot and all six rows were updated: ranks 54/57/65/77/80/106 became 57/59/68/82/85/113, and the underlying ratings, confidence intervals and vote counts were revised with them. Ratings moved by at most one point, within the +/-2 to +/-6 intervals, so the changes are leaderboard drift rather than a change in product quality. Two newer listings on the same board were again seen and deliberately NOT added as rows: grok-4.5-text (rank 47, 1465 +/-4) and deepseek-v4-pro-high-20260813 (rank 53, 1464 +/-7). This registry carries one representative exact listing per product family, and the site's generators key rows by tool_slug, so a second row for the same family would silently overwrite the first in every generated comparison rather than adding evidence.

sources.name: Arena-Rank methodology
sources.measures: Bradley-Terry ratings with reweighting and confidence intervals from pairwise preference data.
sources.use_for: Explaining how Arena scores are produced
sources.caveat: Human preference can reward style and verbosity; it is not an objective factuality test.

sources.name: SWE-bench Verified
sources.measures: Percentage of 500 human-validated real GitHub issues resolved by a coding model or agent.
sources.caveat: Scores depend heavily on the agent harness. mini-SWE-agent v1.x and v2.x results are not directly comparable. Checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28: the site still publishes a machine-readable results payload (an embedded leaderboard-data block covering Full, Verified, Lite, Multilingual and Multimodal). The Verified group is unchanged at 180 rows dated 2023-10-10 to 2026-02-26; the newest is still a mini-SWE-agent 2.0.0 run on Gemini 3 Pro at 69.6% resolved, and the highest score in the group is Sonar Foundation Agent at 79.2% (2025-12-05). No Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Replit, or other tracked end-user product appears in that Verified set, so no product-level coding row is added from it. The page text still confirms the 500-instance human-validated subset.

sources.name: LiveBench
sources.measures: Objective, frequently refreshed tasks across reasoning, math, coding, language, instruction following and data analysis.
sources.caveat: Always state the release; questions and model configurations change between snapshots. Checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28: the repository is live and active (latest commit 2026-09-26), but its public changelog still ends at 2026-01-08 and the README still shows "Top models as of 30th September 2024". A dated leaderboard can be read without a browser through the app's client-side data route: the app's release list still ends at 2026-06-25 and serves table_2026_06_25.csv with 63 model rows across 23 tasks, alongside categories_2026_06_25.json covering the same 23 tasks in 7 categories. An earlier check of the same dated file recorded 58 models; the current file holds 63, so either the publisher re-uploaded the table or the earlier count was wrong - the 63 figure is the one verified against the file today. Newer model configs keep appearing in the repository (gpt-6-sol-max, gpt-6-luna-max, grok-4.7) without a matching published table, so treat LiveBench as release-pinned evidence, not a current ranking.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis methodology
sources.measures: Independent intelligence, latency, speed, price, speech, image and video model evaluations.
sources.use_for: Cost/speed context and non-text modality methodology
sources.caveat: API model measurements do not equal the complete end-user product experience. Re-checked 2026-09-28: the methodology page is live and still serves no dated per-model score table, so no Artificial Analysis row exists in this registry.

sources.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1 leaderboard (frozen; subdomain now serves 4.0)
sources.measures: Accuracy of an agent + model + reasoning-effort configuration on 89 complex containerized terminal tasks.
sources.use_for: Coding agents and terminal-capable development tools
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14, re-checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28: https://www.tbench.ai/leaderboard/terminal-bench/2.1 returns a 308 redirect to https://www.tbench.ai/?version=2.1, and every route on that host - including ?version=2.1 - serves the Terminal-Bench 4.0 board (title "Terminal-Bench 4.0", leaderboard slug "4-0-0", board updated_at 2026-09-21T21:28:10Z, 27 rows at 330 trials each). No 2.1 rows could be read from this URL on any date, and no archived 2.1 board exists on the site. The 4.0 board lists only Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build and mini-SWE-agent configurations and carries no Cursor, Copilot or other tracked-product entry. Never present this as a model-only score; keep agent, exact model, effort, trial count and integrity metadata visible.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Image methodology
sources.measures: Blind pairwise image preference with exact model/version and matched prompt conditions.
sources.caveat: Keep text-to-image and editing pools separate; old model versions are historical evidence only. Re-checked 2026-09-28: the page is live with separate text-to-image and editing sections and still serves no dated score table.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Video methodology
sources.measures: Modality-separated video quality, latency and price comparisons.
sources.caveat: Do not compare Elo across different video modalities or output settings. Re-checked 2026-09-28: the methodology page is live and states that each modality has its own Elo pool in the Video Arena, so silent and audio-enabled outputs are not compared directly and editing is not compared with generation. No dated score table is served.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis TTS methodology
sources.measures: Provider-voice and controlled-voice human-preference comparisons for text-to-speech.
sources.caveat: Controlled-voice and provider-voice arenas answer different questions and must remain separate. Re-checked 2026-09-28: the methodology page is live at its canonical route (https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/text-to-speech); the older /text-to-speech/methodology path returns a 308 redirect to it. No dated score table is served.

sources.name: Terminal-Bench: Cursor CLI + Grok 4.5 submission
sources.measures: Maintainer-verified Terminal-Bench 2.1 submission record for one exact Cursor CLI configuration.
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14, re-checked 2026-09-21 and re-hashed 2026-09-28 against the raw submission file (sha256 a73454861c91299b501637e6df6082f2f16cf9c9f6c98f07bce315189f82eb23, 29,033 bytes, byte-identical on both re-checks): Cursor CLI 2026.07.08-0c04a8a + cursor/grok-4.5 at high effort, 79.33% +/- 1.46, 445 trials, 8.99% reward-hack disqualifications, dated 2026-07-09. Two limits sit on it: the Terminal-Bench 2.1 README states "Community submissions are currently closed for Terminal-Bench 2.1", so the 2.1 board is frozen, and the live 4.0 board carries no Cursor entry, so there is no current Cursor reading to compare it to. Scores from 2.1 and 4.0 are different harness versions and must never be compared with each other.

sources.name: Harbor Hub — Terminal-Bench 2.1 dataset
sources.measures: The live dataset record for Terminal-Bench 2.1: which tasks the frozen board ran and which version is published.
sources.use_for: Confirming the task set behind a Terminal-Bench 2.1 configuration score
sources.caveat: Checked 2026-09-14, re-checked 2026-09-21 and re-checked 2026-09-28: the dataset page describes "Version 2.1 of Terminal-Bench", and the Terminal-Bench 2.1 repository independently holds 89 task directories, matching the 89 tasks this page reports. The earlier wording that Terminal-Bench 4.0 is a "larger" task set is not supported: the current Terminal-Bench repository holds 66 task directories at its v4.0.0 release tag (published 2026-08-26). 2.1 and 4.0 are different task sets, not a small/large pair. The Hub's latest published revision is now 2.0.2 (revision 6), above 2.0.1 and 2.0.0. This page publishes the task list, not leaderboard scores; it cannot upgrade a 2.1 score into a 4.0 score.

coding_agent_snapshot.note: Maintainer-verified configuration snapshot, re-hashed byte-identical on 2026-09-14, 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-28. The Terminal-Bench 2.1 board is closed to new submissions and carries no later Cursor entry, and the current Terminal-Bench 4.0 board lists no Cursor configuration at all, so this remains the most recent published Cursor reading and is only valid for the 2.1 task set.

snapshot_summary: Arena Text published a new snapshot dated 25 Sep 2026 (vote cutoff 2026-09-25T22:00:00Z, 8,528,723 votes across 409 models), replacing the 13 Sep 2026 snapshot this file previously pinned. All six tracked listings were re-read from it and all six keep the same exact model version as before. Every rank moved down 2-7 places and every vote count rose, because the new snapshot adds a fresh battle window on top of the old one. Three ratings were unchanged to the point of the board's rounding and three moved by one point, against confidence intervals of +/-2 to +/-6, so this is leaderboard drift rather than evidence that any product got worse.
